messages:
alex: Quick alert from the new private cluster: after applying the tightened egress netpols we lost HSM-origin audit events for ~12m. KMS calls still succeed for traffic routed via iptables nat on the gateway, but audit sink shows gaps. anyone on call?
priya: Which netpol did we apply exactly? did we restrict hostNetwork or node egress too aggressively?
sam: I pushed infra/netpols/vpc-lockdown.yaml earlier, it's meant to deny all egress from kube-system and infra except to 10.200.0.0/22 (HSM) and 10.200.4.0/24 (logging-proxy). Might've missed the hostNetwork pods.
luca: If the audit shipper runs as hostNetwork=true and the netpol only selects pods, hostNetwork bypasses kube netpols. But iptables on the node could still block based on owner labels if we applied a global egress chain. Did we push a host-level iptables shim?
alex: ops-bot shows a change: etchost-scripts applied a FORWARD chain rule at 3832144300 to clamp outbound from infra nodes to 0.0.0.0/0 -> DROP. That was part of the host-hardening playbook.
priya: Aha. The HSM path uses an egress proxy at 10.200.4.5 and we had a SNAT rewrite so packets to 10.200.4.5 should go out, but the FORWARD rule matched before nat and dropped them.
sam: Can we see the iptables-save from gateway node-04? I suspect the DROP is too early.
sec-bot: config-change: host-hardening/playbook applied by ops-runner at 3832144295. audit-id: phb-2026-03-21-9.
alex: pasted iptables excerpt:

```
-A FORWARD -s 10.50.0.0/16 -d 0.0.0.0/0 -j DROP
-A FORWARD -s 10.50.0.0/16 -d 10.200.4.5/32 -j ACCEPT
```

alex: Notice the DROP comes before the ACCEPT in policy order on the gateway; it never gets to the accept rule.
luca: order bug. We should prefer specific allows before broad drops. Fix: insert accept rule higher or use iptables -I with index 1.
priya: While fixing, we need to rehydrate missing audit events. Any local shipper caches?
sam: /var/log/hsm-audit/ on nodes had rotated tarballs. Check node-04 and node-07. Also our append-only object-store sink (s3://redwood-audit-appendonly) has partial uploads; multipart parts may be pending due to TLS pinning mismatch after certrotate.
sec-bot: incident-detected: 3832144300-3832145020 partial audit gap. severity: high. owners: @alex @priya.
priya: Immediate remediation steps: 1) reorder iptables accept for 10.200.4.5, 2) restart shipper on affected nodes (restart should push cached chunks), 3) run HSM audit replay to SIEM.
alex: Doing step 1 now: `iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s 10.50.0.0/16 -d 10.200.4.5/32 -j ACCEPT`
ops-bot: applied command on node-04 at 3832145740. rc=0
luca: Good. After that, confirm connectivity: `curl -v https://10.200.4.5:8443/health --resolve 10.200.4.5:8443:10.200.4.5`
sam: Also we should harden so this doesn't recur: 1) convert host-level policy to nftables with explicit priority rules, 2) manage gateway rules via a single atomically applied manifest, 3) add CI that tests iptables ordering against allowlist paths in a local vagrant cluster.
priya: RBAC note: during lockdown we removed kube-system->hostaccess clusterrole for logging-sidecar. That prevented the shipper from reading journal on some nodes; I reverted that binding on node-07 to restore reads. We'll make a scoped role instead.
sec-bot: patch-event: clusterrolebinding logging-hostaccess reverted at 3832145805 by priya.
alex: rehydration logs show node-07 uploaded two tarballs to s3 at 3832145850 and 3832145865. SIEM ingestion resumed. gap narrowed to ~4m.
luca: Post-incident actions: 1) move audit-sink to dual-write (object-store + gcp-pubsub) for durability, 2) require host-level policy manifests to be reviewed by security before apply, 3) create a runbook for "gateway iptables order troubleshooting".
sam: I'll own the CI test that simulates gateway ordering and ensures our egress to HSM flows pass even with default DROP.
priya: I'll create the scoped role for the shipper (read-only journald + /var/log/hsm-audit) and add an admission policy that blocks clusterrolebindings to kube-system without explicit approval.
sec-bot: post-incident: severity downgraded to medium at 3832145905. summary: allowed accept rule applied, shipper rehydrated archived chunks, audited gap ~4m. owners: @alex @priya @sam.
alex: thanks all. I'll open the customer notification draft for review once we finalize timeline and affected tenants list.
